output.methodChoice: Standard-depth diagnostic sequence, applied internally. I collected X7 first (the 26-week baseline that the policy's band rule needs), then X3 (per-rollout pod metrics, to test the one piece of evidence pointing at a release fault). I did not use any other catalogue items.
output.brief:
Don't roll back, and don't mute alerting.

Last week's 0.41% is an ordinary swing. The previous 26 weeks averaged 0.35%; the policy's upper limit is 0.48%. Five of those weeks were higher, and the three investigated turned up nothing. The burn-rate page was nowhere near firing (0.82x against 2x). The dashboard matches raw logs, and bookings didn't fall (41.0% to 41.2%).

Dario's new-pod error gap is real but isn't about v4.18: new pods start with an empty cache and time out more for their first 40 minutes in every rollout, even a config-only redeploy of unchanged code. That's 10–20 errors, against roughly 2,300 extra in the week. Nobody has compared same-age pods on different versions, so I can't prove v4.18 is clean. The replica move and partner-sync's month-end run are unchecked.

Next: record the week as normal, leave alerting alone, and run the standard check on the week of 2 Nov. Investigate only if it exceeds 0.48% or stays high. Consider showing the 26-week band on the dashboard's default view. I'm about 80% sure 'no action now' is right; the rise's cause remains unknown.
